sections.title: AI Agent Applications for Dallas Organizations
sections.description: Production AI agent solutions for DFW's leading organizations.

blocks.heading: Mortgage and Real Estate Document Agents
paragraphs: DFW is the US's most active residential real estate market — autonomous document processing agents create significant value:

Mortgage origination agents: Autonomous agents processing incoming mortgage loan applications — extracting income documentation, ordering appraisals, triggering credit report pulls, verifying employment, and assembling the complete loan file for underwriter review without manual data gathering.

Title examination agents: Agents researching public property records, identifying liens, easements, and encumbrances for DFW's large title insurance operations — automating the research phase of title examination while flagging exceptions for licensed title officer review.

Construction loan draw agents: Autonomous agents processing draw requests for DFW's large construction loan portfolio — verifying inspection report completion, calculating eligible draw amounts, and routing for lender approval.
Cost: $55,000–$140,000 | Timeline: 12–22 weeks | Texas property law context

blocks.heading: Healthcare Prior Authorization Agents
paragraphs: For Texas Health Resources, Baylor Scott & White, and the large PA processing community serving DFW's hospitals:

PA submission and monitoring agents: Autonomous PA assembly and submission for DFW's major commercial payers (BCBS Texas, UnitedHealth, Aetna, Cigna) — building documentation packages, submitting electronically, monitoring status, and escalating denials to appeal workflows without manual follow-up.

Texas Medicaid prior authorization agents: PA automation for Texas Medicaid and CHIP managed care plans (Superior Health Plan, Molina Healthcare of Texas) — incorporating Texas-specific prior authorization requirements and HHSC managed care program rules.
Utilization management agents: Autonomous utilization review for DFW's large health systems' inpatient and outpatient authorization programs.
Cost: $55,000–$145,000 | Timeline: 12–24 weeks | HIPAA BAA

blocks.heading: Supply Chain and Logistics Agents
paragraphs: For AT&T (Dallas HQ), American Airlines (Fort Worth HQ), Toyota North America (Plano HQ), and DFW's large corporate supply chain community:

Supplier performance monitoring agents: Autonomous agents tracking delivery performance, quality metrics, and financial health signals for DFW's corporate supply chains — generating proactive alerts when supplier risk thresholds are exceeded.

Freight tracking and exception agents: Agents monitoring shipment status across DFW's large logistics network, proactively identifying delays, and initiating exception resolution workflows for AT&T's and American Airlines' complex logistics operations.

Purchase order and invoice matching agents: Autonomous three-way match for DFW's high-volume corporate AP operations — matching POs, goods receipts, and invoices and routing only exceptions to human reviewers.
Cost: $50,000–$130,000 | Timeline: 10–22 weeks

blocks.heading: Energy Operations Agents
paragraphs: For Atmos Energy (Dallas HQ), Oncor Electric (Dallas HQ), and DFW's utility community:

Customer service automation agents: Autonomous handling of routine customer service requests for Atmos and Oncor — account changes, billing inquiries, service scheduling, and outage reporting — reducing call center volumes while maintaining customer service quality.
Field service coordination agents: Agents coordinating field technician scheduling, work order assignment, and completion tracking for DFW's large utility field service operations.
Regulatory compliance reporting agents: Autonomous compilation and validation of PUCT (Public Utility Commission of Texas) and pipeline safety regulatory reports for DFW's regulated utilities.
Cost: $50,000–$130,000 | Timeline: 10–22 weeks | PUCT regulatory context

blocks.heading: Enterprise Procurement Agents
paragraphs: For CBRE (Dallas HQ), Tenet Healthcare (Dallas HQ), and DFW's large enterprise procurement community:
RFP response agents: Autonomous agents gathering vendor capability information, preparing standardized RFP response packages, and comparing vendor responses for DFW's large procurement organizations.

Contract renewal monitoring: Agents tracking contract expiration dates, monitoring vendor performance relative to SLA commitments, and generating renewal recommendation packages for procurement managers.
Cost: $50,000–$130,000 | Timeline: 10–20 weeks
